reason: Sunlight can evaporate seawater, beginning the route back to shore as fresh water.
expectation: Water will evaporate from the sea, leaving dissolved minerals behind.

effect: Evaporation has started the freshwater cycle, leaving most dissolved minerals in the sea.
reaction: The distinction between evaporating water and the minerals left behind is satisfying.
reason: Cooler air should condense the evaporated water into clouds.

choice.with: Cooler air high above the surface

expectation: Water vapor will condense into cloud droplets.

effect: The evaporated seawater has condensed into a cloud, advancing the freshwater route.
reaction: The separation of water from dissolved minerals is clear.
reason: Wind can carry the cloud toward land so its water can return to the shore.
expectation: The cloud will move toward the coast.

effect: The cloud has moved over land, positioning its moisture to return to the shore.
reaction: The connection between sea evaporation and rain over land is clear.
reason: The rocky rise may lift the cloud and help produce rain over land.

choice.with: A rocky rise behind the shore

expectation: Air rising over the rocky rise will cool and produce rain.

effect: The cloud has produced rain on the rise, ready to flow back toward the shore.
reaction: The role of rising air in making rain is clear.
reason: The slope should guide rainwater downhill toward the basin and shore.

choice.with: A slope toward a broad basin

expectation: Fresh water will flow down the slope toward the shore.

effect: The stream returned fresh water to the sea, completing the first goal.
reaction: The return to low ground neatly closes the water cycle.
reason: Moonlight is reflected sunlight, so these two objects suggest the remaining goal.

choice.with: The Moon with a pale early crust

expectation: Sunlight reflecting from the Moon will produce moonlight.

effect: Reflected sunlight provides the moonlight needed for the remaining goal.
reaction: The distinction between reflected light and leftover heat is useful.
reason: A calm night at the sheltered pool suggests a place to see the reflected moonlight.

choice.with: A calm night at the sheltered pool

expectation: Moonlight will appear in the still pool.

effect: Reflected sunlight has no available combination now, so I need another route to the moonlit scene.
reaction: I’m surprised the direct pairing did not work.
reason: Inspecting the calm night should reveal what can be used to set up the pool scene.

choice.inspect: A calm night at the sheltered pool

expectation: The inspection will show a compatible object, possibly the tidal pools.

effect: The inspection automatically made a still pool at night; the pool scene is now prepared.
reaction: The automatic combination clarified the setup after the failed direct pairing.
reason: The still pool and reflected sunlight suggest the remaining moonlight scene.
expectation: Moonlight will appear reflected in the still pool.

effect: The still pool reflected the Moon, completing the remaining goal and the chapter.
reaction: The quiet reflection is a fitting end to the journey.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following seawater through evaporation, rain and runoff was worthwhile: it made the water cycle and the separation of dissolved minerals clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed attempt to combine reflected sunlight directly with the calm night was confusing, though the subsequent inspection clarified the setup.

surprise.text: I expected moonlight to combine directly with the calm night, but the tidal pool first had to be made still.

arbitrary.text: The need to prepare the pool before adding moonlight made sense afterward, but the failed pairing did not explain that requirement.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the water-cycle sequence connected familiar processes clearly, and the final reflection gave the landscape a quiet ending.
